items.title: A Behind-the-Scenes Look at Esquire’s Party for the 20th Anniversary of the Big Black Book
items.snippet: At the Ludlow House on the Lower East Side, a bunch of New York’s coolest people gathered to raise a glass to the essential guide to style and luxury.

items.title: 3D Genome Atlas Reveals Early Roots of Schizophrenia
items.snippet: How does the human brain wire its reward and motor centers before birth? Using 3D genome sequencing across nearly 287,000 brain cells, UCLA scientists mapped the developing basal ganglia from mid-pregnancy to infancy, pinpointing how spiny projection neurons carry early genetic risk for schizophrenia.

items.title: Autism Shapes How Words vs. Numbers Drive Risk Decisions
items.snippet: Words vs. numbers: A University of Tokyo study reveals that adults with autism spectrum disorder are strongly influenced by positive or negative verbal framing—such as "possible" versus "unlikely"—rather than underlying percentages when making medical decisions.

items.title: Blood-Brain Barrier Protein Atlas Unlocks Alzheimer’s
items.snippet: Does Alzheimer's start outside the brain? Gladstone Institutes researchers mapped the first atlas of 92 blood proteins that cross the blood-brain barrier, discovering that the barrier shuts down the import of protective liver proteins before it ever begins leaking toxins.

items.title: Why political fights devolve into wars about words
items.snippet: In August 2024, I moved with my family from Chicago, Illinois, to Milan, Italy, to test out living overseas for a year.
